title: Blackbox gains rule-packet primitive — compressive compilation without typed-graph weight
content: Blackbox (transcript-search) gains a new primitive: rule-packets as a first-class memory entity. Schema: {signature, generators, predicates, anomalies, flags, witness_examples, version, supersedes}. Storage alongside remember/learn/decide, with its own verb (proposed: bbox_packet or bbox_theory). Render pipeline extended to emit: (a) prose for humans, (b) sigil-ese/JSON for agents, (c) structured AST for a deterministic evaluator. The evaluator is a Rust module in transcript-search (not an LLM) — applies rules mechanically, returns predictions + fired-rule-citations + counter-terms on failed reduction. Self-audit primitive: bbox_packet_verify(packet, dataset) returns fidelity report. Merge primitive: bbox_packet_merge(A, B) produces unified packet with MDL compression check. Rule-packets compose via graph-walk: one packet's signature can reference another packet's predicates (layered theories).
rationale: Empirical validation from E8 + E9 + E10 shows rule-packets produce 40-50x compression with unbounded generalization, merge cleanly across two independent encodings with compression gain (not loss), self-audit faithfully (115/115 on merged packet), and can self-flag corruption/noise when asked. This adds daystrom-graph-like semantic capability to blackbox WITHOUT adopting the typed-graph complexity. Blackbox stays "daystrom lite" while gaining the key architectural primitive (compressive compilation of observations into portable theories). The evaluator being a Rust module (not an LLM) is crucial — it's what makes this a cheap, deterministic infrastructure piece rather than an expensive LLM-in-the-loop. LLM cost is one-time rule-extraction; arbitrary downstream consumers apply the packet mechanically.
